_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy P1, November 2025 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Mathematical
Literacy questions hang off shared scenario boxes: the scenario (tables, graphs, plans and maps
described in bracketed words) is the 'context' of the first sub-question of each block and applies
to the sub-questions after it. memo_answer gives the guideline's working and final answer with
decimal commas kept; the guideline's mark codes (M method, A accuracy, CA consistent accuracy, RT
reading from table, C conclusion, O opinion, S simplification, R rounding) and level tags are left out.
FORMAT: 100 marks, 2 hours, four compulsory questions (Q1 22, Q2 27, Q3 23, Q4 28). ANSWER SHEETS for
2.2.2, 2.2.3 and 3.2 are printed at the back of the question paper. Graph answers (2.2.3, 3.2) are

questions.text: Joyce’s salary is R20 600,00 per month. Last year her monthly salary was R20 000,00. Calculate the inflation rate.
questions.topic: Finance: interest and inflation
questions.memo_answer: Inflation rate = price difference ÷ original amount x 100 = (R20 600 - R20 000) ÷ R20 000 x 100 = 3%

questions.context: QUESTION 4 | 4.1 The invoice given below lists cleaning materials bought by Lily. [INCOME AND EXPENDITURE. Columns: description | quantity | litres | price per litre | cost. 1. Water-based general purpose cleaner | 2 | 25 | R99,00 | R4 950; 2. Pine fragrance disinfectant cleaner | 2 | 25 | R95,00 | R4 750. Sub total ...; VAT (15%) R1 455; Total due ...]
questions.text: Calculate the total cost for ALL the material bought by Lily, including VAT.
questions.topic: Finance: profit, break-even, interest and inflation

questions.text: Lily states that the profit she makes from selling ONE 25 litre (25ℓ) Pine fragrance disinfectant cleaner is R450,00, if she sells a litre at R135,00. Verify, showing ALL calculations, if her statement is VALID.
questions.topic: Finance: profit, break-even, interest and inflation
questions.memo_answer:
Profit = income - expenses = R135 - R95 = R40 per litre; R40 x 25 = R1 000
INVALID
OR cost = 25 x R95 = R2 375; income = 25 x R135 = R3 375; profit = R3 375 - R2 375 = R1 000; INVALID

questions.text: The graph below shows the cost and selling price of all-purpose cleaner material per litre. [Graph COST AND SELLING PRICE OF ALL-PURPOSE CLEANER: number of litres (0-30) on the horizontal axis, cost/selling price in rands (0-4 000) on the vertical axis; a straight INCOME line from the origin and a less steep straight EXPENSES line starting at about R250; the lines cross at point W at 5 litres.] (a) Give the value(s) of the point marked (W) on the graph and explain the meaning of that point. (2) (b) Write down the formula for Lily's expenses if she must pay rent of R200. Cost = ... + ... (2)
questions.topic: Finance: profit, break-even, interest and inflation
questions.memo_answer:
(a) W(5; 675). The income is equal to the expenses (break-even point).
(b) Cost = R200,00 + R95,00 x number of litres

questions.text: Below are the March Test results for nine Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy learners. The test was out of 75 marks. 15 60 75 67 68 73 60 75 58 The teacher claimed that the range of the class is 80%. Show by means of calculations whether the teacher’s claim is VALID or not.
